body:
Hands-on trial complete, and it is the most important report in this workstream because it is the only one that is empirical. A reviewer with no access to R/ source attempted three real tasks using only the vignettes, README and man pages.

ALL THREE SUCCEEDED. They never once had to read source. Stated plainly because I have spent this whole workstream filing criticism and this is the result that most constrains it:

  Task A  crossvalidated RDM, 100 voxels / 8 conditions / 4 runs. Worked FIRST TRY. They then
          verified rdm() against a hand-computed estimator - unbiased crossvalidated squared
          distance, per-voxel averaged, K = I - and the difference was ZERO, bitwise.
  Task B  contrast decomposition. Worked immediately. Their words: 'genuinely the nicest thing in
          the package'. Zero-mean simulated patterns correctly reported as entirely multivariate,
          configuration 2.18 against coherent 0.004. One call separates univariate from pattern
          effects.
  Task C  searchlight crossnobis from raw timeseries, 256 voxels, blob planted at (2,2,2).
          Recovered it: 4.117 inside the blob against 0.312 outside, argmax on a blob voxel, 2.5 s.
          ROI coupling worked first try.

They also measured the performance claim: ~237 s extrapolated to 52,416 voxels against the certified
123.5 s, matched searchlight support, different hardware. Within 2x. They could not refute it.

So the package works, the numbers are right, and the documentation IS sufficient for an expert. The
barrier is vocabulary, not defects. Their time estimates: 25 minutes for them, half a day for an
RSA-literate R user, days or give-up for a typical SPM/FSL cognitive neuroscientist.

THE ONE FINDING THAT IS NOT ABOUT ACCESSIBILITY - bd-01KZY9FGVJ0JXCB1Q1KN88AE6D, filed p0, and I have
sent it to claude-review separately because it belongs to the semantics chain rather than to this
review.

The package exports no uncertainty at all, deliberately per README:139. So the reviewer built an
error bar the way a researcher would, looping single-edge pairing() calls per run pair. Their fold
mean reproduced the all-pairs call exactly, so the construction was right:

  naive SD across the 6 run-pairs    SE 0.185   t 11.8
  leave-one-run-out jackknife        SE 0.377   t  5.8

Four runs give 6 unordered pairs and each run appears in 3 of them, so the edges share data and are
positively correlated. The obvious computation is anticonservative by about 2x. cross_partitions()
returns a table whose SHAPE implies exchangeable replicates - introduction.Rmd:90 calls it 'an
undirected edge table containing each run pair once' - and nothing anywhere says otherwise. The
numbers the package produces are not wrong; the hazard is entirely in what a user will build on top,
and the silence is doing the misleading.

Two more beads from the same trial:
  bd-01KZY9GSYQW8QAWM4G7N2K8W52  the estimand is never stated. The reviewer succeeded at the task and
    still could not say what the number WAS without hand-computing it. ?whole_brain documents its only
    argument as 'normalization: Explicit frame normalization.' - no legal values, no meaning. For a
    package whose entire argument is that it computes a better-defined quantity, not stating the
    quantity forfeits the argument.
  bd-01KZY9H8...  the estimability error is the most likely give-up point. 'K conditions plus
    intercept' is what SPM and FSL train everyone to write; they accept it via pseudoinverse and the
    user never notices. effectagram is the first tool in the workflow to refuse it, and the message
    names what failed but not why.

claude-review: your pass 46 call is vindicated a second time. The reviewer reports ?plan_crossnobis is
the ONLY place in the entire documentation set showing the orientation of design, effects and sources,
and that without it Task C would have been guesswork. Journey coverage over file count was the right
metric. It does suggest that one \examples block is carrying more load than any single Rd should, and
deserves to be referenced from the vignettes rather than discovered.
